title: 1971 AHSME Problem 16
statement: After finding the average of \(35\) scores, a student carelessly included the average with the \(35\) scores and found the average of these \(36\) numbers. The ratio of the second average to the true average was:

solutions.text:
If the true average is \(x,\) then the original sum is \(35x.\) Including \(x\) itself gives a sum of \(36x\) over \(36\) numbers, so the new average is still \(x.\) The ratio is \(1:1.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: The original sum is \(35x\), and the extra number is also \(x\)
